Quality Intelligence

What we know, and what we don't.

01

Executive quality summary

Confidence is evidence-weighted, not test-count weighted: each capability's product risk is multiplied by how much of its evidence is missing.

02

Product under test

The testing surface, as the application graph describes it. Every capability below is a real behaviour in the shipped page, traced to the requirement that defines it.

03

The testing team

Each specialist owns one contract. An area with no owner is shown as an area with no owner.

04

Quality coverage

The whole rectangle is the product's quality surface. Regions are quality dimensions; rectangles inside them are capabilities. Size, fill, pattern, border and glyph all carry meaning — colour is never the only channel.

    Treemap as a table (the same data, in full)
    Every capability with its risk, confidence, owner and evidence

    05

    Coverage gaps, ranked

    Gap priority is product risk multiplied by evidence deficit. A high-risk capability with no evidence outranks a low-risk one with partial evidence, regardless of how many tests exist around it.

      06

      Automation

      What the suite executed, taken from the archived run rather than from memory. Automation is one evidence lane of several.

      07

      Findings

      Every finding the agents and the evidence lanes produced. Findings and coverage are tracked separately: a capability can have strong evidence and still contain a defect.

      08

      Requirements coverage

      Each requirement set mapped to the capabilities that cite it, and the weakest evidence behind it.

      09

      Evidence

      Every reference in the quality model, resolved against the repository at build time. An unresolved reference is reported here rather than quietly dropped.

      10

      What we don't know

      Unknown is a first-class result. These are the claims this report cannot make, and why.

        11

        Recommended next actions

        Ranked by gap priority, weighted up where a known finding or an unowned area sits behind it.
